text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) This is a great concept. I never purchased the original fitbit because I wanted a heart rate feature. The problem is the heart rate accuracy during CrossFit/HIIT/strenuous-type exercises. The accuracy is spot on during the day, and seems equally accurate during mundane exercises (running, cycling, rowing machine, etc). The inaccuracies show up during virtually any other style of workout. I have corresponded a substantial amount with fitbit, and they say they are working on improving the algorithms. Who knows if they can figure it out.

While I would like to see it being accurate during my workouts, one of my biggest complaints regarding it's accuracy is the "lag time". Meaning, how long after the activity is over does the fitbit take to begin showing an accurate heart rate. I would think a few seconds is reasonable. Well, it takes 30-45 minutes!! I don't understand why, and fitbit was unable/unwilling to tell me why. I have tried wearing it on both wrists, at varying tightnesses and locations on my wrists, and taking it off for a few minutes and then putting it back on. Nothing helps, it still takes 30+ minutes for it to be accurate again.

So how is it inaccurate? It reads REALLY low. It will typically read 50-60 bpm low during and immediately after an intense workout. My actual heart rate is 160-180 and the fitbit will say 95-110.

I gave it 3 stars because everything else about it is great and useful. So if your workouts are walking/running/cycling or other similar types of activites, it will work great for you. For those doing similar exercises as me, it will only be useful for monitoring heart rate throughout the day and while sleeping. I decided that was useful enough to keep it, though it was close. It becomes a personal decision as to the value of it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish I purchased this knife as a semi-impulse buy. I had been looking for a new edc for a couple months, however I was skeptic to stray away from my kershaw of 5 years.

After my initial purchase I read many mixed reviews, and after a month of carrying here are my thoughts.

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish

text_fidelity_a: 350W Electric Skateboard with Wireless Remote Control I am an old lady, not a skateboard person, but my neighbor is a divorced dad who gets his two boys every other weekend and because he has a roommate to help pay bills, I know he doesn't have a lot of money to spend on his kids when he gets them, so on occasion I have gotten a few things for them because I'd rather hear kids laughing and having fun than whining at their dad because he can't afford to buy them all the newest, coolest things.  So having said that, my intentions are also to benefit me, too!  I took this over before the boys were to be dropped off and he was so happy - I did apologize that I couldn't get two of them but hoped they would share.  About an hour later I heard them squealing so figured their dad had brought out this skateboard and was preparing to read them the riot act if they didn't share.  I looked up in time to see the older boy - he's maybe 10 or so - zoom past my house and the grin he had just made me laugh.  He was obviously loving the ride!  He came zooming past again and in another couple of minutes, the younger one - I think 7 or thereabouts - zoomed by.  His eyes were wide and he had the biggest grin on his face!  That's really all I wanted to see - that they liked it and I believe their dad was so happy to have a cool thing for them to play with at his house.  I mean, I can't say how it feels to be on it or anything like that, but I can say that two little boys had a fun weekend with their dad riding, I'm pretty sure, was their first ever skateboard and it was motorized and could be controlled with the remote control to boot!  If you are a grandparent or a parent of a young person (10 or younger, in my opinion), this skateboard is going to be a perfect gift for Christmas or their birthday.

text_fidelity_a:
Nautilus E618 Elliptical Machine I'm a runner looking to get back into racing shape. The Nautilus E618 Elliptical Machine will help me get there.

For those who haven't an elliptical machine, it is somewhat like riding a bicycle standing up without a seat up a hill. Exactly how steep the hill is you decide. Similar muscles are exercised as far as your legs go.

Added also in the mix are the arms. The Nautilus E618 Elliptical Machine is no different. Imagine two ski poles. The motion is like that. Depending on how you grab it, the intensity of the arm workout, and with that, your core.

This is a real workout that will tire you in ways regular running cannot. For the runner looking to strengthen his endurance and body overall, this is good tool. Your knees will appreciate the break.

The Nautilus E618 Elliptical Machine has several important numbers on the display. Speed, distance, calories burned, and pulse rate. Meanwhile, there are several workouts to choose from (once you get in shape -- these aren't easy).

You can have as many as four profiles so if you are a multi-athlete household (as we are), this is nice. I've set mine to reflect my body size so that calories are better figured and that I can track my progress without confusing it with anyone else using the machine.

All of this can be transferred and processed through an app. You can then look at the data nicely presented on a website.

It took around three hours to put together. When it arrived, I had the delivery guys bring it fully boxed to my basement, to my workout room where I have a treadmill, some minor weights and other equipment. It is heavy and they needed a dolly.

Where it lacks is that the speakers are weak as is the fan. In my opinion, both are useless. I cannot offset both with a room fan and through Bluetooth speakers. Meanwhile, the distance counted seems off (much less than expected). I'm hoping there's a solve for that, but it is frustrating.

Anthony Trendl
americanspeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Nautilus E618 Elliptical Machine

text_fidelity_a: Fishing Hat Sun Protection UPF 50+ Cap with Breathable Mesh Safari Hats for Men Women - Dark Grey This Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection is a nice hat and one I’m glad to have. We live in a warm weather state and time at the pool and beach is a must. But that also means exposure to sun both directly and indirectly. I have sensitive skin - and we all need to be careful of sun exposure - so I learned from my dad to wear a hat as often as you can. I gabbed this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection to protect my head and face and so far, it’s working great. I like the color - it’s a black, though not stark, but a bit of a “faded” black. I have another, similar hat that the top stands “taller” than this - I’d describe this one as “streamlined” which is fine. I really like the venting around the head for keeping my head cool, but still protected. There is a “band” that goes around the inside - I think it’s for protecting the forehead from sweat - which is fine - I do not feel it. There is also the ability to tighten the area around the head to make it tighter. I do not need this - I’ve got a pretty big head - but if my wife were to borrow it she might - we have not used this option yet. I’ve worn it in the pool and it worked great. It cannot protect from the reflective light, but it keeps the sun off my head and that’s what I’m looking for - and for that it worked perfectly. I do take the “strap” and tuck in up over the sides and into the tightener strap at the back to keep it out of the way. If you needed it for keeping the hat on, however, it’s there. Overall this is a nice hat and I’m really glad I got it. I will most certainly get a lot of use out of this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection.
text_fidelity_b: Fishing Hat Sun Protection UPF 50+ Cap with Breathable Mesh Safari Hats for Men Women - Dark Grey

ONTEL Chill Chest Cooler – 60 Cans, Collapsible, Insulated, Lightweight, Portable, Waterproof – Great for Parties, Picnics, Camping, Beach, Tailgating, Fishing, Hunting, Boating and More! ...But let me say, I was underwhelmed when I unpacked this from the huge Amazon box in which it arrived. Chill Chest is comprised of hinged or interlocking panels of some kind of extremely lightweight plastic foam - it's not waterproof (there are relatively large spaces between the panels, in the seams, around the hinges, etc.), nor is it terribly attractive and it squeaks when the panels rub against eachother. Since I haven't actually used the Chill Chest yet, I can't speak to its durability but from the looks of things, I'm wondering if that's going to be disappointing too.

To be honest, I was primarily interested in getting this product as a way to keep hot things hot. During the Christmas holidays it seems like there's always an opportunity to engage in that frustration-inducing, logic-defying necessity of taking perfectly good, hot food out of the oven, swaddling it in layers of towels, and driving it miles away to a friend's or relative's home, all the while keeping my fingers crossed that it will still be a little hot when we arrive. Sadly, the heat-trapping methods I've tried so far don't do much - so I'm hoping this contraption may be just what me, the family's amateur "caterer" ordered.

I have tried it on 5 different brands of SUP boards and each time it has been consistent. Filling up each board to 15 psi within 9 to 9.5 minutes. I have pumped up 3 SUPs in a row without any issues. It doesn't heat up the pump or hose nearly as much as others I have tried. Took this pump out on labor day to the beach. But instead of using my vehicle to pump this up I bought the Jackery Portable Power Station Explorer 300 (Which is smaller than a toaster). Just be careful not to get sand or dirt in the connections so they get a tight seal.

One note I would like to mention. When I tried this pump with the 12v in my suv and the engine wasn't running the pump did preform at a slower rate about 11 minutes for 15 psi. I would recommend you have the engine running if you want the pump to perform at the better time around 9 minutes.

For comparison my boards are 10.5 feet and 33 inches wide. I also have an 11.5 foot also.

I also want to caution you, that there are other pumps that look exactly like this pump being sold on Amazon. Externally they may look the same but the motor/pump inside is not the same thing and does not pump them up nearly so quickly, they also heat up a lot more.

text_fidelity_a:
LEBBOULDER Gym Gloves/Workout Grips: Quality Neoprene Pads for Men & Women’s Weightlifting, Crossfit Training, Fitness or Exercise Unfortunately, these just didn't work for me so I had to send them back. On the plus side, they're surprisingly well made for the cost. I used these regularly for a few weeks, rinsing them off by hand after every workout and throwing them in the washing machine a couple of times, yet they never showed any wear and tear. The padding on the palms was sufficient to prevent callouses from forming, which is the main purpose of hand protection for me for the gym.

Unfortunately, these were just too big. I'm a woman, 5'2", with hands proportional to my height. Other reviews mentioned having extra material on the palms, but I decided to risk trying these anyway since many buyers reported that this wasn't a big deal. That part wasn't a major problem for me either, but the finger loops were way too big. Also, I found that my palms tended to get sweaty while wearing these, though that decreased a bit over time; eventually, I think I would've gotten used to them and not sweated with them on, or at least not so much. Still, the oversized grips plus the tendency for my palms to sweat meant that I couldn't get a good grip, especially when lifting heavy or doing swings. That's why I ultimately returned them.

Although these didn't work for me, I think they could be a good option for those with slightly larger hands. If you're of at least average height, you'd probably be okay with these. And even if you're not, the generous return period means that you have enough time to test these for yourself at no risk. I understand that offering different sizes would likely mean a price increase, but I hope the company is able to do this one day. If they maintained the build quality, a small price increase would still make these grips good value for money, and I'd jump at the chance to buy a slightly smaller version of this product.
text_fidelity_b: LEBBOULDER Gym Gloves/Workout Grips: Quality Neoprene Pads for Men & Women’s Weightlifting, Crossfit Training, Fitness or Exercise

COAST® HP7 650 Lumen Focusing LED Flashlight with SLIDE FOCUS® and BEAM LOCK®, Black In the past, I've mostly used Maglite. But this little beauty really puts any Maglite I've had to shame. Honestly. . . I don't know a lot about "lumens". . . but I just know that this thing is BRIGHT. When it says that it's a "focusing" flashlight, that means you can put a spotlight one sometime. Depending upon how far away the item is, you pull the ring on the light end out to where you want it to be for your spotlight. Using this feature will cut-down on your battery life, but the batteries last from 5.75 - 10-hours, so quite a long life.

Please see the other coast flashlights as well. They make them without the "focusing" part, if you wish, but there is so little cost difference that I think it's a nice feature to have.

The packaging is really nice. A slick box. The flashlight comes with a nice carrying case, as well as strap.

It feels really durable and sturdy in your hand. Small and compact.

The on/off button is on the back end. At first I thought I wouldn't like that so much, but now it feels fine. It just depends upon what you're doing, because if you're holding it pointing down, the you can use your thumb to turn it on/off. If you're holding it out, then depending upon how coordinated you are, you might have to use two hands to turn it off.

This flashlight is an investment. It's not something you're going to get at the 99 cent store. But it should last you a very long time.

text_fidelity_a:
Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe I read so many raving reviews about this Fort Knox safe that I waited for months for them to come back into stock (the entire internet was sold out!). Once they finally came back onto Amazon ("The Safe Place" was the vendor), I immediately bought one. Upon examination, the safe itself was very well built. Quality metal and extremely sturdy. Then it came time to program the combination.... Oh my, what a mess. As others have stated, the combination is kind of difficult to figure out. You need to completely unscrew and remove the lock from the safe to reprogram it, which is a mess because it's underneath a layer of foam padding totally covered in glue (which gets EVERYWHERE).

The problem for me started once I did manage to get the combination reset and put back into the safe. For whatever reason, although the combination part of the lock was functioning fine, the actual unlocking mechanism on the safe kept failing. What this resulted in was the combination working (click!), but the safe failing to unlock. Humorously enough, while I was packing the safe back up to return it, it spontaneously burst open when I turned it on its side. Thinking perhaps it had fixed itself, I tried relocking it and reentering the combination. "Click!"...... Stuck locked again....

So, it did end up going back. Unfortunately, the vendor wouldn't pay return shipping on it, and this thing is HEAVY, thus it cost a fortune to ship it back. This thing ended up costing me a whole lot of time, effort, and money, and I'm glad it's gone. With so many positive reviews, I have to believe that I may have just received a lemon. The vendor offered to exchange it for me, but I was too nervous to lock valuables inside of even a new one, with the fear lurking inside me that whatever I put in there may stay there for good. I am giving it two stars though, because even though it didn't work, the build was very impressive, and had it worked, I would have loved it.
text_fidelity_b: Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe

Operator error, actually. But I didn't come here to assess blame. No. I came here to praise the Ozark Trail 12 Can Expandable Top Soft-sided Cooler.
I had had the previous cooler for years and years and years. Could not tear it up. Took Bubba to do that. So within an hour of burying the last one I came here to see if the thing still existed. I found many similar coolers, the most expensive costing $300. At that price it should have come with a complimentary built in solar refrigerator. Alas, it did not. Just an ordinary cooler with a very recognizable trendy logo.
After a time I saw that indeed the son of my cooler DID exist in the form of the Ozark Trail 12 Can Expandable Top Soft-sided Cooler. I pounced.
This early morning before daylight (late summer) it sits just beyond this room stuffed with ice and water for another excursion to the jungles, less Bubba this time. You can't kill the thing unless you drag it behind an ATV, car, or possibly a boat. Unless you demand Goochie Brand sneakers to go to the opera, you'll be more than pleased with this excellent cooler. Fact. And yes, I have seen the crappy reviews. I have no idea.

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor Edge Brush Demon - Tactical Survival Outdoor Knife with 13.5" Carbon Spring-Steel Blade and Rubberized Non-Slip TPR Handle This knife was designed for Outdoor Edge by Jerry Hossom, a highly respected big knife expert who makes some awesome custom knives for big bucks. (Search the internet for "American Kopis" and you will see what I mean) His biggest emphasis is on self-defense and martial arts.

This particular knife is really cool looking and immediately inspires confidence when holding it in your hand. To check out how it functions I compared it to one of my Esee Lite machetes, a big knife that I have used for hundreds of hours after trying out several other large knives/machetes/hatchets/saws trimming trees and cutting brush. The Esee can be found for between $60.00-$70.00 and the Brush Demon is available from $50.00- $70.00, close enough for comparison purposes. The Esee is made in South America and has a lifetime guarantee. The Brush Demon also has a lifetime guarantee and is made in China.

The Esee has micarta handles, a blade length of 17.25", an overall length of 23.5", a blade thickness of .065", and weighs about 17 oz. The Brush Demon has a rubberized handle, a blade length of 13.5", an overall length of 20.08", a blade thickness of .160", and weighs about 18 oz. Both blades use a medium grade carbon steel that is black powder coated. These carbon blades are tougher, durable, easy to sharpen, but also susceptible to corrosion.

Blades are a bit like cars: some people like one design, some like another, some owners drive their cars gently, and some drive them to the edge of abuse. So when I give you a perspective on a knife, it's simply my perspective based on how I use it. My height, my weight, the length of my arms, how strong I am (or not), and the type of swing I use all come into play. So here is what I found after using both knives to limb trees and to chop into trunks. Most people would probably use hatchets or saws for this type of work but I have found that a big knife is more effective and can be used for a longer time without arm fatigue.

For me, the Esee Lite is the hands down winner. It is about 3.0" longer, resulting in better weight transfer with a full swing. The blade itself is about 4.0" longer and is markedly thinner and sharper. Having a blade that is less than half as thick as the blade on the Brush Demon results in more energy being driven deeper into the wood. If you compare the cut made with the wide blade of a hatchet to that of a good machete, the thinner blade of the machete will always cut farther into the wood with less effort. The same holds true when comparing the thickness of these two big knife blades. I also noticed that the blade configuration of the Brush Demon resulted in a much smaller "sweet spot" when cutting wood. The best cuts were made when the wood was impacted at the belly of the blade. Off-center hits were noticeably ineffective. The Esse Lite was better balanced and similar to hitting a golf ball with an over-sized driver--even a relatively poor impact had good results.

So with apologies to Jerry Hossom--and still lusting after an American Kopis--the Brush Demon doesn't stand up to the Esee Lite machete for the type of work I use it for. On the other hand, the pointed Brush Demon would probably do much better against soft targets--especially for stabbing. If I could only carry one survival knife with me, it would still be the Esee.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Edge Brush Demon - Tactical Survival Outdoor Knife with 13.5" Carbon Spring-Steel Blade and Rubberized Non-Slip TPR Handle

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor A winner at last. I like it and recommend it. My F11 was a confusing, hard-to-read, and somewhat inflexible Polar monitor. This FT60 makes up for those past frustrations. The display uses bold characters and is easier to read. No longer do I have to deal with those awful timed training sessions such as Normal 1, Short 1, etc., ad nauseum. Now I can exercise as long or little as I like in a week and if I'm being a little too carefree the watch will suggest what I should be doing differently to stay on track to my goals. This monitor is, as you have seen, rather expensive but if you are really serious about wanting to pursue a healthy or more healthy lifestyle I think this is a worthwhile purchase. My only minor complaints are that I dislike Polar's wrist bands as a matter of personal preference. I like a watch to be able to lie flat and face up but you can't do that with the fairly stiff, curved Polar band. A washable woven nylon band would be nice perhaps with a Velcro closure. I wish the monitor's beeps were louder (even when set on Very Loud) as I really can't hear it well but my ears are old so that's just me. I like the accessories available that may be useful to me should I purchase them in the future. I am happy with this purchase and recommend it.

2-YEAR UPDATE:

Well, I've had this trainer for a bit over 2 years. It is still working fine. I've replaced the battery twice myself and did not suffer any problems from that experience. The watch back is a bit hard to unscrew. I have done it with a large flat-bladed screwdriver (really large). The best tool to use is a spanner wrench which is two pointed rods mounted to a crossbar. This makes the back very easy to remove. I got mine here at Amazon. It is sold by Micro-Tools and costs less than twenty dollars. It occurs to me that if you have needle-nosed pliers, you could hold the jaws open just wide enough to fit the tips into the holes around the cover. Twisting the pliers should spin the cover open.

I also recommend putting a little silicone grease on the o-ring before you screw it back together to keep water out and to make it easier to remove next time. Don't bother trying to remove the o-ring too as it is fragile. Leave it in place on the battery cover and just smear a bit of grease on the cover's threads and the surface of the o-ring. Don't use petroleum jelly.

I know from reading the reviews that some folks have had disastrous problems after replacing the battery. I've found that my watch remembers all my workouts and training data after replacing the battery. I did have to enter the date and time again. If you have problems after changing the battery you can try a 5-button reset. Just hold all the buttons down for maybe 15-seconds (I'm a little fuzzy on how long exactly; the procedure is in the manual, though) and the watch should come back to life and will only lose the date and time. I have heard good things about Polar support if you get into real trouble. I've heard it is a waste of time trying to e-mail them. The way to go is just to call them.

I've replaced the battery in the transmitter once and I'm not sure it really needed it but it seemed like a prudent thing to do after a year. No problems with that at all.

I still like this monitor very much. I feel that Polar supports it well with their website and forum. Also their training videos are informative and helpful. The training programs are sensible and I have lost weight and built up my stamina using this product. It still looks like new. Unfortunately, the crystal is a cheap piece of soft plastic and easy to scratch. I only wear my watch during workouts so I have only a few scratches. If you are going to wear this a lot you might want to take precautions against scratches. (Plastic polish does a good job of mitigating the scratches.)
text_fidelity_b: POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor

SecurityIng® Waterproof 3 Modes 600 Lumes Mini LED Bicyle Light Bright Headlight Lighting Lamp with 4.2V Rechargeable Battery Pack for Camping, Cycling, Riding It took a long time for me to find the right light on amazon, this one fit my criteria well.
1. this is compact
2. it doesn't have a huge battery that will get in the way.
3. It is bright. Im not positive about the 1200 Lumens, but it is as bright as my 900 lumen NR.
4. It is light weight. nothing like my other light,
5. I wanted an actual mount, not a rubber band.

I was skeptical about this light because of the following reasons:
-The name seems suspect. - not a name brand i recognized
- other reviews stated they had problems
-the mount looks super trashy and bulky

After getting the super mini light, I found it to be well made, and it came with a more compact mount than the one picture on amazon. if you go to the sucurityING website, the correct mount is shown. The light output is amazing. the light gives you a lot of down and side light, as well as distance lighting spot beam. it was well appreciated on the trail last night. It has a nice metal housing, and big button in back for high, low, and high-flash. which is really bright, and i don't see using that ever. The charger seems to be of low quality, but it works. my only ride so far has been an hour on high beam.

The only complaints i have are as follows:
1. the battery cable comes detached at the connector with vibration. I had to tie the connector together, and this problem was resolved. make sure you fasten these together, because there is nothing like going down a trail at night when your light goes out. luckily i was on a straight section of trail.
2. The mount takes a bit of getting used to, make sure it is really tight, otherwise it will move. it is hard to get real tight because of the weird mounting clip, vs screw. it worked though in the end. I would have preferred a twist tighten mount.

Overall, this is a great little light for the money. I am happy with my purchase, but cannot say anything about durability as of yet. i would recommend this and other SecurityING products.
text_fidelity_b: SecurityIng® Waterproof 3 Modes 600 Lumes Mini LED Bicyle Light Bright Headlight Lighting Lamp with 4.2V Rechargeable Battery Pack for Camping, Cycling, Riding

2 in 1 LED Headlamp Flashlight Combo, 150 Lumens, Ultralight Waterproof, 1.2oz,Compact, Full-metal body, for Running, Camping Hiking, Cycling, Kids,ONLY 1 AA battery req & Incl 1 Energizer AA.COLORDAY 5/26/22 Still my everyday carry light, still going strong. Still waterproof, still gets dropped occasionally and comes back for more. I've worn most of the anodizing off down to bare aluminum. It's not a flamethrower, but for 99% of my needs, 80 lumens for 5+ hours is way more useful than 1500 lumens for 10 minutes. This light just keeps on trucking.

2/20/18 Still going strong, my everyday carry light.

1/16/17 Bumped up to 5 stars, the replacement light has been perfect. I lubed the tailcap threads and O-ring with petroleum jelly as soon as I received it, this might help.

11/15/16 Colorful Days replaced the light even though it was beyond the warranty period, quite nice of them. Will see how long this one lasts. Back up to three stars for now.

11/7/16 Downgraded to one star. Light flickers and is quite dim. Reacts to tailcap being unscrewed or tightened, and sometimes only works after loosening the tailcap slightly. Poor connection between tailcap and body of the light - useless.

So far so good. Solid little light and significantly less expensive than the Fenix and 4Sevens and Zebralight flashlights I keep losing. Headband is comfortable. The little case is nice enough but no one is ever going to keep the light in it - 5x more bulky than the light and headband alone.

With the cost reduction vs the brands mentioned above, some compromises are made. While it runs on rechargeable batteries, it's not really happy doing so. Much dimmer. I don't think the regulation circuitry likes the lower voltage much vs primaries much. The claim of 150 lumens is a joke, WAG compared to other lights I have, I would put this at ~80 lumens.

Can't comment on durability or waterproofness yet.

So far, while I'm happy with the light for the money, there's a reason I bought higher end lights. If my better lights don't turn up soon I'll just buy another one and this light will eventually get relegated to backup duty.

text_fidelity_a:
Push-Up Pump [[VIDEOID:mo2U0MH5NGR4RTX]]This is a great little push up device. It's easy enough so that anyone can do a push-up or two with it, even your grandma. But, it also gives your upper body a really good workout even if you can do a lot of push-ups.

I really like how this device encourages great posture and discourages hyper-extension of joints. Push-ups would be a nearly perfect exercise if people didn't hyper extend their joints or over strain their weak parts when doing them. This device fixes everything by using your body weight to give you exercises that you can actually do.

This has helped me a ton with my upper body strength. It works, and I definitely recommend it.

Now, for the negatives.

The tension bands are a joke. Unless you either cut them apart or use all 65 lbs of them, they'll make a horrible snapping noise. You'll end up just throwing these away.

This won't last forever. It's not the sturdiest construction, and the design puts some weird strains on some of the joints, so it's only a matter of time before this falls apart. But you should get about a year of good use out of it, and by that time you'll be doing push-ups on your own.

The legs/feet of this should have been about twice as long, to make this sturdier. As it is, the only balanced position is with the seat placed on my upper stomach. If they were longer, then I could pick where I wanted to place my body on this.

And dismounting takes a lot of practice, and the fabric part peals off the first day you use it.

But overall, I'd heartily recommend it, especially if you've always dreamed of being able to do a lot of push-ups. No matter what your fitness level, this will definitely push you to the next level with push-ups.

Pros:
+Great way to work up to doing push-ups
+Great way to rapidly increase the number of push-ups you can do
+Fits away easily in a corner
+It's sturdy enough for what you need it for

Cons:
-You won't ever use the tension bands
-It's not the sturdiest construction. Expect it to break after about a year of use.
-Comes with fabric that's warping and pulling off
-The legs should have had more surface contact with the floor, to make this more steady
-I fell off this quite a few times when trying to stop doing push-ups, so it will take some time to get used to dismounting this device
text_fidelity_b: Push-Up Pump

text_fidelity_a:
Bayou Fitness Total Trainer 4000-XL Home Gym I've been using the total trainer for about 9 months now and I'm finally comfortable leaving my thoughts on it. Overall, I think this is the best value in a Total Gym type of machine and I would not hesitate to recommend it to others. I love mine.

---------------------------------------
Pros:
Huge glide board

Large range of resistance settings

Ability to add free weights

Comes with a curl bar (though I found it less than useful for actual curls) and other attachments that you may find useful.

Great price to performance ratio

Cons:
Some limitations for strength once you get into better shape, but with true, proper form which makes the exercises much harder and humbles guys who think they can really bench 260lbs because they hold the weight and move their arms 10 inches up and down 5 times in a row, this machine will last most average or out of shape people for quite a while.

The video that comes with it is pretty lame in my opinion, you're better off searching youtube for demonstrations of exercises on a Total Gym and doing those.
---------------------------------------

The machine can support up to 385lbs, so if you're 180lbs and add 100lbs of weights, you're still way under the limit. The maximum resistance levels are 69% without the glide board pulley engaged and 38% with. So technically, at 180lbs, the maximum resistance you're going to get is 106lbs and 193lbs. That sounds like a lot, but keep in mind that most of the common exercises seem to work better with the pulley engaged (and some would be impossible without it since the cable/rope is a fixed length and way too long to use without the pulley to take up the slack). For example, the instructions show you a way to kneel on the board, attach the mini-pulleys to the glide board and do a bicep curl with the curl bar. This is pretty unstable at resistance level 11 (the board wants to slide out from underneath you and you're really pulling yourself high into the air (I hit my head on my basement ceiling trying the exercise this way). While trying to keep the board from moving around underneath you is a decent way to work your core, it detracts from the exercise. I've found that bicep curls work best with the pulley engaged and the user hanging upside down, curling the fly handles up towards the chest (search [Total Gym upside down bicep curls] on youtube for an example). Still, for most people who are not in great shape, curling 106lbs isn't easy with good form (arms straight down at the sides on every rep reset, curl all the way up to the chest keeping the wrists straight and the elbows at the sides near the hip as much as possible). You could also invest in a weight vest to wear and increase the overall weight. Bayou Fitness could solve this issue by providing another, shorter cable that would allow certain exercises like the upside down bicep curl, chest fly, upright row and so on to be done without the middle glide board pulley being used.

Also, I'm not sure I'd bother with the squats on this machine, they don't allow you to have proper form because the glide board restricts movement (search [proper squat form] on youtube or Google to see what I mean). For some people the movement on this machine might not be a bad thing, but in my case, it causes pain in the knees whereas normal, proper form squats do not.

For those than cannot do a pull-up to save their lives, this machine can help with the large muscles involved (shoulders, biceps, triceps, upper back), but only actual pull-ups will work the stabilizer muscles. Still, if you're upper body is pretty weak or out of shape, this will get you more than 4/5 of the way there with the extra 100lbs (again, provided you use proper form and pull your elbows down towards your hips and keep your shoulders up and back and your head up during the exercise). Eventually, you'll need to start doing actual pull-ups to work the stabilizers and your core to get real results.

The instructions show a method of doing a bench press using the side pulley attachment points and thereby NOT using the middle pulley, which gives you a max resistance level of 69% of your body weight + 100lbs of plates on the bar attachment (this should be able to allow anyone up to about 230lbs to at least bench their own weight). However, the method they describe actually promotes improper form (but a slight adjustment will allow good form provided you aren't too wide). on a bench press, you want the bar to come down towards your nipple area, not your neck or collar bone (doesn't work the chest well and can produce injuries). Your elbows should be bent down towards your hips or sides. If you're willing you slide your body up on the board so that the side pulleys line up with your nipple area (which leaves your head hang off the board a bit and makes the cables come up underneath your armpit area but allows the proper motion for a bench press) you can get a decent bench. Two things with this. 1, don't wear loose shirts when doing this, they will get caught up in the pulley and 2, always keep the footboard attached for this exercise in case you cannot finish a rep, simply put your foot straight down to catch your body and there's no way for the bar to trap you or crush your chest. In essence, this allows you to bench as much as the machine will take without a spotter and without the same risk of injury that comes with lifting free weights on a bar (if you have good form otherwise you'll get injured even if you don't fail the lift). I do wish that the bar was wider for those of us with longer arms (closer grip stresses the triceps instead of the chest). There may be some ways around that last limitation, but I haven't found one that ensures that the cables will not slide on the bar that is also completely safe. zin theory, you could get a regular free weight bar and two 2.5lb slotted plates to thread the cable heads through so they don't move, but then you're adding 5lbs of weight plus a 25-45lb bar, which makes the exercise a bit more dangerous.

The few suggestions I'd make to Bayou Fitness would be a shorter cable to allow certain exercises to be done without the pulley, a wider curl bar to help isolate the chest when using that for benching and the ability to add more than 100lbs to the glide board weight bar. I'm not sure if the last one is possible (I'm assuming that the limitation is based on the strength of the bar and not the glide board), but the other two should be no problem. But overall, for most people looking to get into better shape, this machine and adherence to proper will get you there provided you put the time into it.
text_fidelity_b: Bayou Fitness Total Trainer 4000-XL Home Gym

text_fidelity_a: LEE PRECISION Lee Preciesion 90999, Single Stage Press, Classic Cast Breech Lock I studied long and hard on whether to purchase this fine heavy duty Lee Cast Iron Breech lock press. I have used many presses over the last 40 years and still own some of the finest ones made. I was introduced to the unique breech-lock system 2 years with their hand press. The additional cost of bushings is somewhat of a downside but outweighed with speed of die change over. I have replaced all of Lee's rubber "O" ring lockrings due to their instability and lack of accurate repeatable settings. Hornady's  side lock clamping and Forster rings are far better and do not mar the 7/8"X14 threads due to frequent adjustments. My use of the Breech Press was another press for more mundane belling,universal decapping,expander mandrels and case forming of pistol and 300 B.O. This usage for me reduces the number of needed breech lock adapters. The only fault that I have found is that the shell holder mounting slot is pointed to the right of the press opening sharing the same slot to allow the primer kicker arm to deflect spent primers into the scrap tube. I find that by using the shell holder opening pointed to the left during use with a right mounted handle will sometimes push the shell holder to the right thus dismounting the shell holder. I wish that Lee would modify the right sided shell holder installation slot to the middle and re-mill the area and still keep the primer deflector as is.All in all 5 stars for sure and a great product. The ram is solid with no sloppiness at the top of stroke.
text_fidelity_b: LEE PRECISION Lee Preciesion 90999, Single Stage Press, Classic Cast Breech Lock

text_fidelity_a:
AUTRUN Colorful Replacement Accessory Clip Clasp Strap for Flex 2 I got a Flex 2 and these magnetic holders in the same order because I wanted to keep it in my pocket rather than on my wrist, just as I had been using the Fitbit Flex for years. Unfortunately the Flex 2 wouldn't track my sleep. I tried all of Fitbit support's recommendations multiple times (reset 3x, reinstall app, change sleep sensitivity, etc.), but nothing helped. I didn't try the notification settings but knew vibration worked because it vibrates when you reset it. So I exchanged the Flex 2 for another.

The next Flex 2 didn't track sleep either, and it didn't vibrate! I knew this because when I put it in the charger and pressed the reset button it didn't vibrate. I tested all the notification settings to make sure, and repeated all the support procedures but still no sleep tracking OR vibration. So I exchanged it for a third one.

The third one was EXACTLY like the second one...no sleep or notifications! *sigh* I have been using a Flex in my pocket for years and didn't want to lose that. So, I would give it just one more try. I sent the 3rd one back and then went to Walmart for a 4th one. Maybe Amazon had a detective batch?

The 4th still didn't track sleep, but it did vibrate when I reset it! Maybe this time resetting it would fix the sleep tracking? No! Then I noticed that it did vibrate when I pressed the reset button but not when I turned on notifications. What the?Then I happened to try notifications again with it out of the holder and it worked! Then I put it back in the holder and it didn't work. Ah ha! Maybe it was the magnet all along! I cut off the "tail" of the holder with the magnet and tried it again. This time it vibrated, but very lightly. That's when I discovered that there is a second magnet in the holder. I had assumed that the little studs inside the holder were just metal for the magnet to stick to, but they are in fact a magnet as well. Could this have also been the problem with the sleep mode all along?

I tossed the holder and put the Fitbit in the small wristband and put that in my pocket. Now EVERYTHING works exactly as it's supposed to. So now I know. The magnets in these holders breaks the Flex 2's sleep mode and notifications...and it only took four Fitbits to find that out! I cut off the straps of the included band and now use that as a holder in my pocket. I didn't want a "clip" holder anyway so that will work fine for me.

I hope this saves someone the weeks of irritation and wasted hours that I went through.
text_fidelity_b: AUTRUN Colorful Replacement Accessory Clip Clasp Strap for Flex 2

text_fidelity_a:
LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction I've had this for a couple of months, but just used it for the first time this past weekend while camping with friends. I will never use it for that again.

A) The wide angle sounds like a good thing, but it was really annoying to my friends. I had to keep the headlamp at the lowest possible brightness, and even then the light shining so wide was still annoying to everyone around me.

B) The led strip is very thin, resulting in the light source being behind the plane of my glasses. So much light was reflecting off the lenses of my glasses back into my eyes that I truly couldn't see much of anything in front of me. There's no point lighting a path if I still can't actually see the path.

Also, this headlamp has a proprietary charger. So you have to keep that specific single-use cable with you in order to recharge the batteries. And the batteries drain even when not in use. I charged it fully when I first got it a couple of months ago. Fortunately I tested it before my camping trip and discovered it was completely drained. So you can't just charge it and expect it to be ready when you need it. I had to fully charge it just before I left.

It is really very bright, so if you need something really bright, and you don't have glasses, and there's no one else around you who might be blinded by your headlight, then it might be an ok choice for you. But with so very many options out there, I recommend you keep looking. There are definitely better choices than this.
text_fidelity_b: LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction

3V Recon Tanto First off I have to say that I bought this Cold Steel Recon Tanto from another source at half of the price offered on Amazon. But after removing it from the packaging and handling it for a while, I can tell you that even at the Amazon price, this is a great value. Yes, you can buy a better version of this knife from Jake Hoback, but you will be spending almost three times the money for incremental improvements. In my case, I would have had to pay five times the money. Like most collectors I have several "safe queens" but at this price I don't feel bad about using and abusing this well-made tool.

Your first glance at this knife will confirm its utilitarian/industrial good looks. It is obviously a knife that is built strongly to be used in tough tasks. Don't bother confirming the blade sharpness with the paper cutting test, you can simply look at the edge under a good light and see the small serrations that line the cutting edge. If you want to be bold and test it with your finger, TREAD LIGHTLY! Cold Steel has taken a thick piece of steel and tapered it into a razor-sharp blade. You will even be able to feel the small serrations pulling at your skin as you touch the edge.

Good useful length, full tang, great balance, sticky rubber grip, this tool inspires great confidence when you hold it. Take a look at some of the posted videos to see what types of abuse this knife has been subjected to and survived handily. If I had to leave our home suddenly and enter the woods and swamp lands of Southwest Florida, I'd probably select my Busse Hellrazor to take with me. On the other hand, if I showed up at a rendezvous point with a Cold Steel Recon Tanto, no one would laugh at me. They know better.

PS: A decent (not great) kydex sheath is included. If you're like me, you don't like a sheath hanging off your belt that can catch on various objects and/or make noise while you're trying to be quiet. A simple band threaded through the lower part of the sheath will keep it secure against your thigh.
text_fidelity_b: 3V Recon Tanto

text_fidelity_a: EdisonBright Fenix CL05 8 Lumen LipLight LED EDC tri-Color Light Emergency lamp (Purple Body) AAA Battery Bundle Ok this light has its share of things that im not overly thrilled with, but it is such a cool light with really cool features.  So lets get the bad out of the way.  First the plastic clear cover isnt great.  It feels a bit on the cheap side and i fear it will either scratch bad or crack.  It is glued to the body and it just looks sloppy.  It would have been nice if they just left it unglued so it could be removed if desired. The diffuser works well but again it would be nice if it was removable.  So thats the bad.  Now for the good.  2 batteries came with mine.  An extra o ring and a decent keychain clip was nice touch.  Great knurling on the twisty end and i liked the attachment ring as it swings easily and lays flat.  Threads are smooth and work well.  Mode 1 is perfect for low level tasks.  Mode 2 is bright and would work well for closeup work or walking in a dark familiar area.  Mode 3 is solid red and will work perfect for astronomy or perserving night vision.  Mode 4 is red flashing, perfect for signaling or warning.  Mode 5 is solid green as is just way cool probably great for map reading but just love the cool factor of green light.  Mode 6  is green flashing.  Once again signaling or warning, and way high on the cool factor.  Mode 7 is white flashing.  Yea not the best mode but at the end of chain so no big deal.  The flashing is about a 1 second cycle so kinda perfect as far as a flashing mode is concerned.  Run times should be more than acceptable.  Other than the plastic cover durability should be amazing.  Twist end works great and cycling thru the modes is smooth and easy.  Weight is great at about an ounce or so.  Im so thrilled with this light.  No its not the brightest light but as far as useful multifunction lights are concerned this one is far and away the best one i have come across.  The price is steep...no getting around that.  If your looking for a bright light, look somewhere else.  Looking for cheap, not gonna find it here.  Want more colors and modes than you know what to do with?  Here it is.  About the only other thing i wish this had would be either blue or uv led.  Nice job fenix nice job
text_fidelity_b: EdisonBright Fenix CL05 8 Lumen LipLight LED EDC tri-Color Light Emergency lamp (Purple Body) AAA Battery Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Glomax Darts Light Up Soft Toss Long dark winter days. Cabin fever. Snowed in. No activity. Kids climbing the walls. What to do...

We're all heading into the basement where we have collected fun games over the years, like an air hockey table, Foosball, electronic darts, an electronic basketball hoop....and now our new addition, the light-up lawn darts game. It is a blast in the basement (although we keep a little bit of lighting on). This is so much fun, and really adds a unique game to break up our wintertime boredom.

Here are a few tips that may help you.

1) We put a few streaks of glow-in-the-dark paint on the rings, to brighten them up a bit, and it worked wonderfully. We got this super bright green glow in the dark paint for about $10 here on Amazon and it worked great: [[ASIN:B00BD63C8W Ultra Green V10 Glow in the Dark Paint 1/2Oz]]

2) Don't give a second thought to replacing the batteries. It's easy. I buy all my replacement button batteries from Amazon. In fact, these lawn darts take the LR41 batteries, which you can get 10 of them from Amazon for about $6: [[ASIN:B000AQ7ME6 Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR41 AG3 192 Pack of 10 Batteries]]. Or if you want more, you can get 50 of them for about $13-14: [[ASIN:B0057ON2JA 50 Pack Maxell LR41 AG3 192 button cell battery "NEW HOLOGRAM PACKAGE "]] .

3) If you need replacement parts, which is honestly unlikely, as these things are sturdy as heck. And if you need information on replacement parts, you can email: replacementparts@franklinsports.com or you can call 1-781-341-5178.

Thanks for reading my review. I sure hope it helped you.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Glomax Darts Light Up Soft Toss

text_fidelity_a:
LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail The other reviews mentioning the finely threaded battery compartment are pretty accurate. The first thing I did when I got mine was wipe down the threads, there was definitely dust that immediately wiped off that I could see being a problem. After it was cleaned I applied a little bit of mineral oil to the threads (probably something better, but it is what I had), and the screwing/unscrewing was much smoother.

Once I added in the batteries and began screwing the cap back on, I could understand why so many people are worried about it. It is really hard to tell if the resistance you are feeling when screwing it back in is because of the spring on the cap, or because it is not threaded well. If you go carefully it should screw back on fine - especially if you clean the threads and apply a little oil.

The laser seems to function exactly as expected, the strobe mode blinks a little faster than I was expecting, but that is hardly a problem.

Will update once it gets some usage!

UPDATE (2 days later): Well the laser started acting weird... Randomly won't turn on, can't rack a shotgun more than a few times without it turning off - and I wasn't even shooting. I'm actually impressed by just how unreliable it is. Going to roll the dice and get an exchange, but my hopes are not very high at this point.

EDIT: I got a second one of these and am pleased to report that it is more reliable. Was able to put a few dozen rounds thru my shockwave with no issue.

I want to give it 5 stars, but considering the problems so many people have had (myself included) I simply can not.
text_fidelity_b: LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail

text_fidelity_a:
Sailnovo Electric Bike, Electric Bicycle with 18.5mph Electric Bikes for Adults Teens E Bike with Pedals, 14" Waterproof Folding Mini Bikes with Dual Disc Brakes [[VIDEOID:e7db44ebf2cc5b42c4a2213aa6e49919]] We really love our new electric bike. The set up was super easy and only required that we remove the packaging, insert the seat, unfold the handle bar, adjust the grip, and screw the pedals in. The recommended initial charge is 5 hours – ours took about 4 hours for the light to turn green.

The bike will provide assistance while pedaling or you can use the throttle on the handle bar to power the bike unassisted. I’m 145lbs and the bike cruises at 12-13mph on flat ground using just the throttle without pedaling. The battery display adjusts according to how hard the assist is working. Pedaling uphill will seemingly drop the remaining charge, but you “gain” it back when the elevation levels out. As far as we can tell, pedaling does not recharge the battery.

I am 5’8” and the bike fits just fine. My husband is 6’4”. He can still ride it but it’s certainly not the most comfortable – much taller than that and you’re likely to hit the handle bar with your knees.

Pro’s:
-Compact enough to fit into a small trunk
-Easy Set up
-3 Pedal assist modes (Mode 1 Full, Mode 2 Partial, Mode 3 Next to nothing)
-Built in headlight, taillight, and horn
-Taillight flashes when braking – even if the lights are turned off
-Comfortable, wide seat
-Rear suspension works great
-Comes with 2 keys and electric functions will not work without the key in place and turned

Con’s:
-Not great for airline travel because the battery is not designed to be removable
-Display shows metric speed and distance only
-A bit heavy
-The manual leaves a lot to be desired – not a lot about the bike BUT its all fairly self-explanatory
text_fidelity_b: Sailnovo Electric Bike, Electric Bicycle with 18.5mph Electric Bikes for Adults Teens E Bike with Pedals, 14" Waterproof Folding Mini Bikes with Dual Disc Brakes

text_fidelity_a:
Nite Ize Spokelit Led Spoke Light - Best Bicycle Lights For Safety And Visibility - Steady Glow Or Flash, Blue Good Stuff: These fit fairly well on traditional spokes, and actually work on my flat/bladed spokes as well (Aksium road wheels). They produce a decent amount of light (I'm using 1 per wheel), and apparently get attention, and I've had the occasional stare or hoot from passing motorists, etc. These increased my side visibility a lot, and I use them on early-morning and night rides. I get a good amount of light from the blinking mode, so I suggest using that to conserve battery unless you're looking for a specific lighting effect, etc.

Bad stuff: The rubber/plastic body is kind of a press-fit on the spoke, so they'll wear down if you're moving them from wheel to wheel a lot--may not stay on the spokes quite as well after a few changes. Putting the light on the spoke also involves kind of a twist-and-slide motion, so you'll want to be kind of light-handed to avoid affecting the wheel's alignment/truing. As other reviewers noted, I got mine in with nearly-spent batteries (one had been on in transit, in the solid-on mode), though I bought the 25-pack-of-2016's, and it's been working OK so far. Also note: if you're riding a bike with narrow chainstays or a narrow front fork, you may want to check the positioning before riding with these--may not have a lot of room between light and frame because of the dome-shaped power button. I was able to make mine fit on a road frame (Orbea Onix), though I have be pretty scientific about where I position the light on the rear wheel.

Overall: for the price, I'd say these are a decent buy, and a relatively low-cost way to get some side visibility.
text_fidelity_b: Nite Ize Spokelit Led Spoke Light - Best Bicycle Lights For Safety And Visibility - Steady Glow Or Flash, Blue

ALPS Mountaineering Lightweight Cot This isn't a folding cot that you can just take out of your trunk, open and sleep on. It has to be assembled each time you use it. The problem with assembly, and the reason that some of the reviewers say that it's easier to assemble after you've done it several times, is that the side rails are approximately the same size as the canvas sleeves you have to put them in. I assume that the canvas will stretch with several assemblies. So when you assemble it, you have to push on it until the canvas stretches to fit the rails. That is no easy task. Once you have inserted the side rails, you have to rotate them. I did that by putting a screwdriver in the holes that need to match up with the slits in the canvas and working it back-and-forth until the rails were rotated. Again, no easy task. Once you do that, you put one end of the spring steel legs in one of the holes of the rails, and compress the spring steel so that you can get the other end in the other set of holes on the other side of the cot. While I was doing this, I was imagining a trip to the emergency room if the spring steel leg slipped out of my hand.

If you can deal with all of this, then it seems comfortable.

I guess it will serve my needs.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Lightweight Cot

text_fidelity_a: Nalgene Tritan Narrow Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottle, Orange w/Blue Cap, 32 oz I always thought these were for city types who spend $1000 on camping gear to spend a weekend in a cabin. Every weekend they invade my small Minnesota town looking for adventure. They've always got the trendy gear and apparel. Most of it is overpriced silliness. I assumed these were the same thing. Boy was I wrong, they are really onto something with these. How can a plastic bottle be so fantastic? First, it's indestructible. I'm pretty sure you could drop one of these from low Earth orbit and it would still be fine when it hit the ground. They don't even get scratched up. I've had one of these bouncing around in the cab of a dump truck for years and it is barely showing wear. These things could be eternal. Second, and most importantly, they NEVER TASTE LIKE SOAP OR PLASTIC! This is my biggest gripe about plastic containers. No mater how much you use them or rinse them, you always taste plastic and you can't get the soap out. These clean and taste like glass. Awesome and worth the $10-12 because they'll outlast anything else

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Steel Creek Fast Pitch Dome Camping Tent with Screened Porch, 6-Person Tent Includes Pre-Attached Poles, Integrated Rainfly, and Screened-In Porch, Sets Up in 7 Minutes This is a good tent. We like the vestibule and sit in it in our folding camping chars when the bugs are out. I can almost stand up straight in the middle (5'9"). We did seam seal everything from the windows down. The rain fly is seam taped from the factory but the tub seam and corner seams leaked a bit after 2 days of rain the first camping trip. I greatly appreciate the reflective guy lines as pictured for reference. The stitching looks good for the price point compared to much more expensive tents. I love the stake out loop at the middle of the vestibule screen door so i can open and close with 1 hand. People complain about things getting wet in the vestibule but maybe they forgot its basically a screened room. Its like an airlock to keep bugs out. We had zero issues with interior condensation after seam sealing. Its roomy for 2, almost a palace. 6 people would be uncomfortable, maybe 3 or 4 at most but for 2 on a queen mattress its basically a bedroom. We uses our camping storage totes as end tables. We like this tent and the vestibule is one of it's best features.

Assembly is a nightmare. After about 30 minutes of adjusting the brake apparatus with no significant improvement, he decided to move the washer for the front brakes to the inner side just to give it a little more braking power by alleviating the gap between the brake and the tire—it was the only thing that worked. I also noticed that the bell on this bike doesn’t have an actual lever that you swing to the side to make a real bell ding—this one has a plastic bit that you hit and you hope it dings and reverberates off the metal circle it’s attached to—it’s not the best bike bell we’ve had.

It does look like a cute bike when everything is assembled, but it doesn’t seem as well constructed compared to our little 12 inch Minnie Mouse bike from Huffy. Strangely enough, some of the protective wrapping for this RoyalBaby bike said Huffy on it, so I’m not sure if this is a division of the larger parent company perhaps? I feel bad giving this 2 stars, but I honestly don’t think it’s spectacular for the money (probably a 3-star bike), but the assembly issues knocked it down to 2 stars, along with the poor instructions. I’ll be sure to buy a pre-assembled bike when we need the next size up.
